title: Candlesticks
hook: Every candle is a decision. Green means buyers won. Red means sellers won.
mission: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to read what a candle's shape actually represents, not just its color.

blocks.heading: Candles show price behavior during a period of time

beats.heading: A tiny story, not a colored block
beats.body: Every candle has a beginning (open), an ending (close), a high point, and a low point. It's a record of what buyers and sellers did during that timeframe.

beats.heading: Pressure, control, movement
beats.body: When you read candles correctly, you stop seeing random shapes and start seeing pressure, control, and movement.

blocks.heading: Two candles, two very different stories
blocks.prompt: Tap each candle to see what its shape actually represents.

left.label: Large green body
left.desc: A large body means price traveled far from open to close in one direction — a decisive win for buyers that period.

right.label: Small red body, long wicks
right.desc: A small body with long wicks means a real fight happened, but neither side settled far from where it started — indecision.

blocks.heading: Is that a safe assumption?
blocks.scenario: A trader sees a candle with a long lower wick and assumes it automatically means the market is about to reverse upward.

options.label: Not on its own — it needs to be read in context, not treated as an automatic signal
options.feedback: Right — a wick shows buyers rejected a push down during that candle, not proof of what happens next.

options.label: Yes — a long lower wick always means a reversal
options.feedback: No single wick is an automatic signal on its own.

blocks.quote: Candles are not just green and red. They show who pushed, who rejected, who held, and where price accepted.

questions.question: Two candles on the same chart have completely different shapes — one is a large green body, the other is a small red body with long wicks. What does the difference actually represent?
options: Different buyer/seller behavior during each candle's timeframe
Nothing meaningful — candle shape is decorative
A guaranteed signal of exactly where price goes next
questions.why: Candle shape is a record of real behavior, read in context — not a prediction on its own.

questions.question: A bullish candle closes ___ where it opened.
questions.why: A bullish close settles higher than the open — that's what makes it bullish.

blocks.prompt: Imagine another AGHF girl asks: "Isn't a candle just green or red?" How would you explain what it's actually showing her?

takeaways: A candle is a tiny record of a fight between buyers and sellers, not decoration.
Body size and wick length both carry information, read together.
No single candle is an automatic signal — context decides what it means.
remember: Every candle is a decision. Read the whole shape, not just the color.
